title: Guaranteed-once ingest proxy with short-lived retry tokens
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: we observe intermittent double-billing for token/embedding requests when client SDKs or gateway components retry after TCP timeouts, LB connection resets, or transient 5xx errors. Current mitigations (client-side dedupe + long-lived idempotency keys) are brittle: keys are often missing, clients open new connections, and long retention bloats the dedupe store. Goal: provide a lightweight server-side layer that converts at-least-once ingestion into an operationally simple 'guaranteed-once' path for billing-critical events without requiring heavy coordination with every client SDK.
background: Incidents: two customer reports in Q4 2024 showed >2x billed tokens for short windows when frontends retried aggressively. Analysis showed request fingerprints were identical but no shared idempotency key was present. Existing ledger reconciliation found duplicates only after the fact, requiring manual refunds. This work follows our billing-integrity initiative to proactively prevent duplicates at ingestion and reduce reconcilers' load.
proposed_solution: Introduce an ingress proxy (stateless-ish) that issues short-lived server-generated retry tokens and enforces a bounded de-duplication window on the ingest path. Key ideas: 1) On first accepted request, proxy returns a Retry-Token header (opaque, HMACed, includes request fingerprint and epoch). 2) Clients include Retry-Token on retry; proxy validates token and dedupes within a small TTL window (e.g., 2 minutes) using a sharded LRU store + bloom filter for memory efficiency. 3) Tokens are lease-like: if a request fails after processing but before client sees response, client can re-send token to fetch result rather than re-execute. 4) For long-running operations or multi-stage pipelines, proxy issues monotonic sequence tickets to allow idempotent append semantics for batched consumption. 5) A background reconciliation job performs ledger-level double-count detection and emits compensating credits if duplicates slip through.
non_goals: Not a replacement for long-term accounting or full two-phase commit across external storages. Not intended to keep indefinite dedupe history; TTL intentionally small to limit storage. Not replacing Dedicated's per-customer fencing, but should be compatible with it.
acceptance_criteria: New ingest path returns Retry-Token on first successful accept for token/embedding endpoints
Retry using the Retry-Token within the configured window returns the original result and does not increment billing counters
System maintains sub-second validation latency for tokens at 95th percentile under baseline load
Memory footprint of dedupe store per shard remains under budget (SRE agreed threshold)
E2E test demonstrates client retry (simulated network drop) causing at-most-once billed tokens in 10k request workload
Reconciliation job detects duplicates with >99% precision and produces compensating credits when applicable

ENG-51791 - implement sharded dedupe store with LRU + bloom filter and HMAC token validation
ENG-51792 - integrate proxy with billing ledger commit path + non-blocking result cache
ENG-51793 - end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (network partitions, dropped connections)

rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood behind feature flag for SDK team (1%)
Phase 1: opt-in beta customers and internal platform services (10%)
Phase 2: gradual ramp to 50% while monitoring duplicate-rate and latency impact
Phase 3: global default rollout with automatic fallback to current path if latency SLOs degrade
Fallback path: if proxy unavailable, clients fall back to original server behavior and emit metric tags to track exposure
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: tokens leak and are replayed beyond intended TTL -> Mitigation: tokens HMACed+bound to client IP/connection fingerprint and short TTL
Risk: proxy becomes latency tail contributor -> Mitigation: lightweight validation, local LRU, avoid cross-shard RPCs on hot path, SLO-based canary gating
Risk: incorrect dedupe causing under-billing -> Mitigation: reconciliation job with conservative heuristics and auto-compensating credits, initial low-percentage rollout
Risk: increased memory/CPU costs -> Mitigation: bloom filter tuning, shard eviction, and adaptive TTL based on load
